items.title: Introducing context-aware rules for AWS Network Firewall
items.summary: AWS Network Firewall now supports context-aware rules, which match traffic by the AWS resources that send and receive it instead of by IP address. A rule can name a virtual private cloud (VPC), a subnet, a security group, or a transit gateway attachment. Rules that match on IP addresses have to keep up with every […]

items.title: Introducing AWS Network Firewall Next Generation policy
items.summary: When it comes to inspecting network traffic, many security teams want two things from a firewall. They want to allow only the traffic each application needs, and they want each allowed connection checked for known threats. Today, you can do both with AWS Network Firewall, a stateful, managed network firewall and intrusion detection and prevention […]

items.title: AWS Network Firewall introduces automated internet firewall mode (Preview)
items.summary: AWS Network Firewall now offers automated internet firewall mode (Preview). In this mode, Network Firewall applies your centrally defined rules to traffic at the internet gateway of each of your virtual private clouds (VPCs). It also performs built-in network address translation (NAT) for outbound-only connections. A subnet that reaches the internet needs only one route, […]

items.title: Introducing AWS WAF simplified pricing
items.summary: Starting today, AWS WAF pricing is easier to predict. Your bill is now based on three dimensions: the resources you protect, the traffic AWS WAF inspects, and the level of protection you apply to that traffic. Existing AWS WAF customers move to the new pricing on February 1, 2027. Until then, you keep your current […]
